#### Why was this blocked?
- **User**: `pawelleszczewicz`

#### How to resolve this:

**Option 1: Get Collaborator Access (Recommended)**
Ask a repository maintainer to invite you as a collaborator with **write permissions** or higher.

**Option 2: Request Permission Override**

#### For Repository Administrators:

---

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Learn more about this security feature</summary>

- Executing malicious code on the deployment server

- Potentially compromising the infrastructure

Preview deployments are powerful but require trust. Only users with repository write access can trigger them.
</details>

[reviewer-agent] Blocking:
- [TC-SEC-002.spec.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/packages/enterprise/src/modules/security/__integration__/TC-SEC-002.spec.ts:151) lines 151-177 do not actually prove recovery-code regeneration invalidates the previous set. The test saves `initialRecoveryCodes[0]`, consumes that code during the first recovery login, then tries the same already-consumed code again after regeneration. That final failure would happen even if regeneration were broken, so the branch still does not cover the invalidation behavior described in [TC-SEC-002-totp-enrollment-login-recovery-codes.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/.ai/qa/scenarios/TC-SEC-002-totp-enrollment-login-recovery-codes.md:31). Keep one untouched code from the original set and assert that it becomes invalid only after `POST /api/security/mfa/recovery-codes/regenerate`.

I confirmed the mandatory gap-mapping check: `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=true yarn test:integration:spec-coverage --json` no longer lists `TC-SEC-002` under `uncoveredScenarioIds`. Existing Playwright evidence in [results.json](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/.ai/qa/test-results/results.json:393) only shows a skipped prior run for this spec, so I did not count that as passing execution evidence.

[reviewer-agent] Blocking:
- [TC-SEC-002.spec.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/packages/enterprise/src/modules/security/__integration__/TC-SEC-002.spec.ts:151) and [TC-SEC-002-totp-enrollment-login-recovery-codes.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/.ai/qa/scenarios/TC-SEC-002-totp-enrollment-login-recovery-codes.md:35): the new test still does not prove that recovery-code regeneration invalidates the previous set. It consumes `initialRecoveryCodes[0]` for the successful recovery login at lines 163-166, then after regeneration retries that same already-consumed code at lines 172-177. That failure would happen even if `POST /api/security/mfa/recovery-codes/regenerate` left every unused old recovery code valid, so step 9 / the expected result “previous recovery codes are invalidated” is not actually covered. Keep one unused code from the pre-rotation set and assert that unused old code fails after regeneration; ideally separate the “single-use” assertion from the “rotation invalidates old set” assertion.

Notes:
- `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=true OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_SECURITY=true yarn test:integration:spec-coverage --json` no longer lists `TC-SEC-002` in `uncoveredScenarioIds`, so the scenario-to-test wiring is present in the enterprise-enabled context.
- I could not run the spec end to end here because `yarn mercato test:integration ...` requires Docker and this runtime has no Docker CLI. `npx playwright test --config .ai/qa/tests/playwright.config.ts packages/enterprise/src/modules/security/__integration__/TC-SEC-002.spec.ts --list` does discover the test successfully.

[reviewer-agent] Blocking:
- The mandatory `TC-SEC-002` gap is not actually closed by this diff. The branch only rewrites the scenario body in [TC-SEC-002-totp-enrollment-login-recovery-codes.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/.ai/qa/scenarios/TC-SEC-002-totp-enrollment-login-recovery-codes.md:24) and the test implementation in [TC-SEC-002.spec.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/packages/enterprise/src/modules/security/__integration__/TC-SEC-002.spec.ts:94), but spec-coverage decides “covered vs uncovered” strictly from case IDs extracted from discovered filenames, not test contents, in [integration.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0048/packages/cli/src/lib/testing/integration.ts:2063). Both the scenario file and `TC-SEC-002.spec.ts` were already present on `origin/develop`, so this branch cannot change the coverage inventory. In this worktree, `yarn test:integration:spec-coverage --json` still lists `TC-SEC-002` under `uncoveredScenarioIds`; with enterprise flags enabled it disappears, which shows the outcome is controlled by env/discovery, not by this rewrite. For a task whose required outcome is closing the `TC-SEC-002` gap, this branch does not change the relevant coverage state.
